claim: Intravital microscopy (IVM) enables live imaging of animals at single-cell level.
source: Intravital microscopy (IVM) enables live imaging of animals at single-cell level, offering essential insights into cancer progression.
evidence: This is a foundational statement about IVM capabilities presented in the abstract.

claim: IVM allows for the observation of single-cell behaviors within their natural 3D tissue environments.
source: This technique allows for the observation of single-cell behaviors within their natural 3D tissue environments, shedding light on how genetic and microenvironmental changes influence the complex dynamics of tumors.
evidence: This describes a known capability of IVM technology.

claim: Traditional uni-parametric approaches often neglect single-cell heterogeneous in vivo behavior.
source: IVM generates highly complex datasets that often exceed the analytical capacity of traditional uni-parametric approaches, which can neglect single-cell heterogeneous in vivo behavior and limit insights into microenvironmental influences on cellular behavior.
evidence: This is a stated limitation of existing analytical methods.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP is a computational framework that enables unbiased single-cell classification based on morphological, environmental, and dynamic features.
source: To overcome these limitations, we present BEHAV3D Tumor Profiler (BEHAV3D-TP), a computational framework that enables unbiased single-cell classification based on a range of morphological, environmental, and dynamic single-cell features.
evidence: This describes the primary function of the tool developed in this study.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP integrates with widely used 2D and 3D image processing pipelines.
source: BEHAV3D-TP integrates with widely used 2D and 3D image processing pipelines, enabling researchers without advanced computational expertise to profile cancer and healthy cell dynamics in IVM data from mouse models.
evidence: This describes a design feature of the tool.

claim: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a highly aggressive pediatric brain tumor characterized by invasive progression.
source: Here, we apply BEHAV3D-TP to study diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a highly aggressive pediatric brain tumor characterized by invasive progression.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DMG tumors.

claim: Distinct migratory behaviors of DMG cells are associated with specific TME components, including tumor-associated macrophages and vasculature.
source: By extending BEHAV3D-TP to incorporate tumor microenvironment (TME) data from IVM or fixed correlative imaging, we demonstrate that distinct migratory behaviors of DMG cells are associated with specific TME components, including tumor-associated macrophages and vasculature.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Tumors comprise many different cell populations that are in constant evolution.
source: Cancer is a complex disease driven by a sequence of genetic and microenvironmental changes. As a result, tumors comprise many different cell populations that are in constant evolution (Vitale et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Tumor heterogeneity differentially promotes key characteristics of individual cancer cells, including proliferation, invasion, and drug resistance.
source: This tumor heterogeneity has important biological and clinical implications as it differentially promotes key characteristics of individual cancer cells, including proliferation, invasion, and drug resistance (Lawson et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Recent spatial transcriptomic and proteomic profiling provides evidence for the existence of multiple distinct microenvironmental niches within one tumor.
source: For example, recent spatial transcriptomic and proteomic profiling provides evidence for the existence of multiple distinct microenvironmental niches within one tumor (Elhanani et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Spatial transcriptomic and proteomic techniques can only provide static information and make use of thin tissue sections that are only one cell layer thick.
source: However, these techniques can only provide static information and make use of thin tissue sections that are only one cell layer thick.
evidence: This describes a known limitation of these techniques.

claim: IVM has provided many new insights into the dynamics of tumor heterogeneity and the development of therapy resistance.
source: Over the past years, it has provided many new insights into the dynamics of tumor heterogeneity and the development of therapy resistance (Scheele et al., 2016; Entenberg et al., 2023; Alieva et al., 2014; Alieva et al., 2019; Alieva and Rios, 2019; Zomer et al., 2022; Alieva et al., 2017; Janssen et al., 2013; Croci et al., 2023; Zomer et al., 2013; Zomer et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Only a small portion of tumor cells is motile in mouse breast cancer models.
source: For example, intravital imaging of mouse breast cancer models revealed that only a small portion of tumor cells is motile (Chen et al., 2019), and that fast- and slow-migrating cells are present in distinct regions of the tumor (Alieva et al., 2019, Bayarmagnai et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Fast- and slow-migrating cells are present in distinct regions of the tumor.
source: For example, intravital imaging of mouse breast cancer models revealed that only a small portion of tumor cells is motile (Chen et al., 2019), and that fast- and slow-migrating cells are present in distinct regions of the tumor (Alieva et al., 2019, Bayarmagnai et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Additional heterogeneity exists among migrating tumor cells that can move randomly or directionally relative to other tumor cells and/or surrounding healthy tissue.
source: Moreover, additional heterogeneity exists among migrating tumor cells that can, for instance, move randomly or directionally relative to other tumor cells and/or surrounding healthy tissue (Alieva et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Traditional IVM analyses have considered cancer cells or the tumor microenvironment (TME) as a homogeneous population.
source: However, traditional IVM analyses have considered cancer cells or the tumor microenvironment (TME) as a homogeneous population, thereby ignoring heterogeneity at the single-cell level and the influence of the local microenvironment, where interactions between neighboring cells may affect cellular behavior.
evidence: This describes a limitation of traditional analytical approaches.

claim: Recent studies have used unbiased approaches using morpho-kinetic parameters derived from live in vitro or in vivo imaging to classify cells.
source: To address these complexities, recent studies have used unbiased approaches using morpho-kinetic parameters derived from live in vitro (Shannon et al., 2024) or in vivo imaging to classify cells and explore the single-cell behavioral landscape as an additional omic layer (Crainiciuc et al., 2022; Dekkers et al., 2023; Freckmann et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: BEHAV3D was previously developed to perform behavioral phenotyping of engineered T cells targeting cancer.
source: In line with this concept of characterizing cellular dynamic properties for cell classification, we have previously developed an analytical platform termed BEHAV3D (Dekkers et al., 2023, Alieva et al., 2024) allowing us to perform behavioral phenotyping of engineered T cells targeting cancer.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: BEHAV3D was initially developed to analyze T cell migratory behavior under controlled in vitro conditions.
source: While BEHAV3D was initially developed to analyze T cell migratory behavior under controlled in vitro conditions, we sought to expand its application to investigate tumor cell behaviors in IVM data, where the complexity of the TME presents distinct analytical challenges.
evidence: This describes the original scope of BEHAV3D.

claim: Significant efforts have been made to develop open-source segmentation and tracking tools for live imaging data, including IVM.
source: While significant efforts have been made to develop open-source segmentation and tracking tools for live imaging data, including IVM (Pizzagalli et al., 2018; Pizzagalli et al., 2022; Joseph et al., 2020; Molina-Moreno et al., 2022; Hidalgo-Cenalmor et al., 2024; Ershov et al., 2022), fewer tools exist for the unbiased analysis of tumor dynamics.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Implementing analytical methods for tumor dynamics often requires substantial computational expertise.
source: One major barrier is that implementing such analytical methods often requires substantial computational expertise, limiting accessibility for many biomedical researchers conducting IVM experiments.
evidence: This describes a barrier to adoption of existing tools.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP expands the capabilities of BEHAV3D by incorporating key features designed for in vivo tumor cell dynamics.
source: BEHAV3D-TP expands the capabilities of BEHAV3D by incorporating key features designed for in vivo tumor cell dynamics (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the relationship between BEHAV3D and BEHAV3D-TP, with reference to Figure 1.

claim: The pipeline includes extensions that integrate tumor cell behavior with spatial features within the native TME.
source: The pipeline includes extensions that integrate tumor cell behavior with spatial features within the native TME, using either in situ (IVM) or fixed correlative imaging to reveal how distinct spatial niches influence tumor dynamics.
evidence: This describes a key feature of BEHAV3D-TP.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP supports a broad range of data formats, including those generated by commercial Imaris and by open-source Fiji plugins.
source: To further facilitate unbiased analysis of tumor dynamics, we developed BEHAV3D-TP as a flexible tool that supports both commercial and open-source data formats, ensuring broad compatibility across different research workflows. The pipeline supports 2D and 3D data formats generated by Imaris and by Fiji plugins such as TrackMate, MTrackJ, and ManualTracking, enabling processing of datasets from the most widely used segmentation and tracking solutions.
evidence: This describes the compatibility features of BEHAV3D-TP.

claim: DMG is characterized by invasive growth and its capacity to spread to other regions of the brain and the spinal cord.
source: Next, we focused on Diffuse Midline Glioma (DMG), a highly aggressive pediatric brain tumor characterized by invasive growth and its capacity to spread to other regions of the brain and the spinal cord (Buczkowicz et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP identified 6 color-coded breast tumor cell behavioral clusters.
source: (b) UMAP plot showing six color-coded breast tumor cell behavioral clusters identified by BEHAV3D-TP.
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1b shows the UMAP plot with 6 clusters.

claim: A total of 935 individual breast tumor cells were tracked.
source: A total of 935 individual cells were tracked.
evidence: This is stated in the legend of Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP identified four color-coded morphodynamic clusters of healthy breast epithelial cells from TEBs.
source: (b) UMAP plot showing four color-coded morphodynamic clusters of healthy breast epithelial cells from TEBs identified by BEHAV3D-TP.
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 2b shows the UMAP plot with 4 clusters.

claim: A total of 291 individual healthy breast epithelial cells were tracked.
source: A total of 291 individual cells were tracked.
evidence: This is stated in the legend of Figure 1—figure supplement 2b.

claim: HR +TEB exhibit greater migratory capacity than HR- TEB.
source: Consistent with previous findings that HR +TEB (Pr-cre/Confetti) exhibit greater migratory capacity than HR- TEB (Elf5-rtTA/TetO-Cre/Confetti), our analysis suggests that this difference is primarily driven by a distinct morphodynamic behavior (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d and is consistent with previous findings.

claim: HR +TEB more frequently exhibited characteristics of Cluster 2, defined by a rounder shape and increased motility.
source: Specifically, HR +TEB more frequently exhibited characteristics of Cluster 2, defined by a rounder shape and increased motility.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of TEB cells.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP identified four color-coded morphodynamic clusters of GBM cells.
source: (b) UMAP plot showing four color-coded morphodynamic clusters of GBM cells identified by BEHAV3D-TP.
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 3b shows the UMAP plot with 4 clusters.

claim: A total of 460 GBM cells were individually tracked.
source: Total of 460 individually tracked cells.
evidence: This is stated in the legend of Figure 1—figure supplement 3b.

claim: Cluster 1 GBM cells, consisting of large and slow-moving cells, were more isolated and located farther from neighboring cells compared to Cluster 6 and Cluster 4.
source: Cluster 1, consisting of large and slow-moving cells, was more isolated and located farther from neighboring cells compared to Cluster 6 (small, fast, persistent cells) and Cluster 4 (very small, static cells).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of GBM cells.

claim: The compact spatial arrangement of small cells within the tumor may contribute to their reduced size.
source: These findings suggest that the compact spatial arrangement of small cells within the tumor may contribute to their reduced size.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GBM data.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP heterogeneity module identified 7 DMG behavioral clusters: retreating, slow retreating, erratic, static, slow, slow invading, and invading.
source: The BEHAV3D-TP heterogeneity module identified 7 DMG behavioral clusters: retreating, slow retreating, erratic, static, slow, slow invading, and invading (Figure 2b–d, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the DMG analysis, shown in Figure 2.

claim: Approximately 10% of the DMG cancer cells were displaying invasive behavior.
source: In fact, in this particular DMG model, approximately 10% of the cancer cells were displaying invasive behavior (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d), in line with the intrinsic infiltrative nature of DMG (Van Ineveld et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the DMG analysis, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: About another 10% of DMG cells were moving back to the tumor edge (retreating, slow retreating clusters).
source: Interestingly, about another 10% of DMG cells were moving back to the tumor edge (retreating, slow retreating clusters; Figure 2—figure supplement 1d), behavior that has been previously observed for glioblastoma and suggested to be regulated by differential chemotactic signaling by the tumor edge and the surrounding brain parenchyma (Alieva et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the DMG analysis, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d, and is consistent with prior observations.

claim: The distinct behavioral patterns were detected in all intravitally imaged mice.
source: Crucially, the distinct behavioral patterns were detected in all intravitally imaged mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d), ruling out any sample bias that might lead to clusters consisting solely of cells from a single tumor or mouse.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: CytoMAP spatial phenotyping analysis identified three different environmental niches: Void regions, TAMM/oligo regions, and TAMM/vascularized regions.
source: Subsequent CytoMAP (Winkler et al., 2009) spatial phenotyping analysis identified three different environmental niches: Void regions (less vascularized and with low glial infiltration), TAMM/oligo regions (enriched in oligodendrocytes, TAMM, and tumor cells), and TAMM/vascularized regions (highly vascularized regions enriched in TAMM; Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a-c).
evidence: This is a finding from the large-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 3.

claim: Invading cells were more abundant in TAMM/vascularized regions compared to Void regions.
source: Interestingly, invading cells were more abundant in TAMM/vascularized regions compared to Void regions that contain a higher proportion of static cells, and TAMM/Oligo microenvironments contain more slow retreating cells compared to the other regions (Figure 3d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is a finding from the large-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Void regions contain a higher proportion of static cells.
source: Interestingly, invading cells were more abundant in TAMM/vascularized regions compared to Void regions that contain a higher proportion of static cells, and TAMM/Oligo microenvironments contain more slow retreating cells compared to the other regions (Figure 3d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is a finding from the large-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 3d.

claim: TAMM/Oligo microenvironments contain more slow retreating cells compared to the other regions.
source: Interestingly, invading cells were more abundant in TAMM/vascularized regions compared to Void regions that contain a higher proportion of static cells, and TAMM/Oligo microenvironments contain more slow retreating cells compared to the other regions (Figure 3d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is a finding from the large-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Single parameters showed a restricted ability to identify differences in cellular behavior among various environments.
source: Interestingly, single parameters showed a restricted ability to identify differences in cellular behavior among various environments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1e–g), underscoring the importance of multiparametric behavioral mapping in revealing more nuanced cellular behavior that cannot be captured solely by individual dynamic parameters.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing single-parameter analysis to multiparametric analysis, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1e–g.

claim: Invading DMG cells tended to be more sparsely distributed relative to neighboring DMG cells compared to static cells.
source: Compared to static cells, invading cells tended to be more sparsely distributed relative to neighboring DMG cells (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1c), consistent with their invasive behavior into the brain parenchyma.
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 4b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Invading DMG cells were found to reside in regions enriched with TAMMs.
source: In agreement with our large-scale TME phenotyping results (Figure 3), invading DMG cells were found to reside in regions enriched with TAMMs (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 4b.

claim: A higher proportion of invading cells were in close proximity to TAMMs compared to static, retreating, and slow-retreating clusters.
source: Specifically, a higher proportion of invading cells were in close proximity to TAMMs compared to static, retreating, and slow-retreating clusters (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Invading DMG cells frequently migrated directionally toward TAMMs.
source: They frequently migrated directionally toward TAMMs (Figure 4d, Figure 4—video 1), suggesting that migration of this behavioral cluster is at least partially mediated by chemotaxis.
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Migration of the invading behavioral cluster is at least partially mediated by chemotaxis.
source: They frequently migrated directionally toward TAMMs (Figure 4d, Figure 4—video 1), suggesting that migration of this behavioral cluster is at least partially mediated by chemotaxis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observation that invading cells migrate toward TAMMs.

claim: All fast-migrating behavioral clusters (invading, erratic, and retreating) were found to be generally closer to blood vessels.
source: Furthermore, all fast-migrating behavioral clusters (invading, erratic, and retreating) were found to be generally closer to blood vessels (Figure 4b and e), suggesting that perivascular invasion is a more efficient movement route for these cells (Figure 4f), a mode of migration that has been previously observed for adult glioblastoma cells as well (Alieva et al., 2019; Wallmann et al., 2018; Ravin et al., 2023; Gupta et al., 2024; Nimmerjahn et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 4b and e.

claim: Perivascular invasion is a more efficient movement route for fast-migrating DMG cells.
source: Furthermore, all fast-migrating behavioral clusters (invading, erratic, and retreating) were found to be generally closer to blood vessels (Figure 4b and e), suggesting that perivascular invasion is a more efficient movement route for these cells (Figure 4f), a mode of migration that has been previously observed for adult glioblastoma cells as well (Alieva et al., 2019; Wallmann et al., 2018; Ravin et al., 2023; Gupta et al., 2024; Nimmerjahn et al., 2004).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observation that fast-migrating cells are closer to blood vessels, and is consistent with prior observations.

claim: Slow-retreating DMG cells were found in regions enriched for SR101+ cells.
source: Lastly, particularly slow-retreating DMG cells were found in regions enriched for SR101+ cells (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d), perhaps reflecting oligodendrocyte-like (OC-like) tumor DMG cells that have been found near oligodendrocytes (Xin et al., 2024).
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale TME phenotyping analysis, shown in Figure 4b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1d.

claim: Slow-retreating DMG cells may reflect oligodendrocyte-like (OC-like) tumor DMG cells that have been found near oligodendrocytes.
source: Lastly, particularly slow-retreating DMG cells were found in regions enriched for SR101+ cells (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d), perhaps reflecting oligodendrocyte-like (OC-like) tumor DMG cells that have been found near oligodendrocytes (Xin et al., 2024).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observation that slow-retreating cells are near SR101+ cells, supported by a citation.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP uncovered behavioral phenotypes that have not been described before and that could not have been identified using single parameter analysis.
source: Using the heterogeneity module of our BEHAV3D-TP pipeline, we uncovered behavioral phenotypes that have not been described before and that could not have been identified using single parameter analysis.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty and utility of BEHAV3D-TP.

claim: The analysis revealed invading and retreating clusters, composed of cells with a similar cell speed but with an opposite migration direction.
source: For example, our analysis revealed invading and retreating clusters, composed of cells with a similar cell speed but with an opposite migration direction, an important biological and clinical difference.
evidence: This is a finding from the DMG analysis.

claim: Bidirectional migration is likely mediated by different chemotactic cues and by the composition of the local TME.
source: Likely, bidirectional migration is mediated by different chemotactic cues and by the composition of the local TME (Kluiver et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by a citation.

claim: Previous studies suggest a major role for the microenvironment in promoting tumor cell spread into the healthy brain.
source: Previous studies suggest a major role for the microenvironment in promoting tumor cell spread into the healthy brain (Taylor and Monje, 2022; Erices et al., 2023; Patel et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The small-scale TME analysis has a higher predictive value compared to the large-scale TME analysis.
source: Our results also show that the small-scale TME analysis has a higher predictive value compared to the large-scale TME analysis, suggesting that a cell's direct microenvironment is a more important regulator of its behavior compared to its macroenvironment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results comparing small-scale and large-scale TME analyses.

claim: A cell's direct microenvironment is a more important regulator of its behavior compared to its macroenvironment.
source: Our results also show that the small-scale TME analysis has a higher predictive value compared to the large-scale TME analysis, suggesting that a cell's direct microenvironment is a more important regulator of its behavior compared to its macroenvironment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results comparing small-scale and large-scale TME analyses.

claim: TAMMs and blood vessels were associated with specific behavioral phenotypes.
source: Indeed, we found that TAMMs and blood vessels were associated with specific behavioral phenotypes, showing the power of BEHAV3D-TP small-scale phenotyping module in identifying novel regulators of cellular behavior.
evidence: This is a finding from the small-scale TME phenotyping analysis.

claim: Slow-retreating DMG cells were found in environments enriched for SR101+ cells, an observation that has not been made before.
source: This is exemplified by our finding that slow-retreating DMG cells were found in environments enriched for SR101+ cells, an observation that has not been made before.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of a specific finding.

claim: Existing literature strongly supports the notion that cell dynamics can serve as a proxy for functional states and phenotypic heterogeneity.
source: While our current study does not provide direct functional validation of the distinct motility clusters identified, existing literature strongly supports the notion that cell dynamics can serve as a proxy for functional states and phenotypic heterogeneity.
evidence: This is a statement about the broader literature.

claim: Prior work has demonstrated that variations in cell motility patterns can reflect underlying functional characteristics.
source: Prior work, including studies by our group (Dekkers et al., 2023, Aragones et al., 2024) as well as (Crainiciuc et al., 2022) and (Freckmann et al., 2022), has demonstrated that variations in cell motility patterns can reflect underlying functional characteristics.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cell morpho-dynamic features have been shown to correlate with differences in cell type identity, T-cell engagement, metastatic potential, and drug resistance states.
source: Specifically, cell morpho-dynamic features have been shown to correlate with differences in cell type identity, T-cell engagement, metastatic potential, and drug resistance states.
evidence: This statement is supported by the preceding citations.

claim: Tumor cell behavior, as captured by BEHAV3D-TP, may serve as a predictive tool for deciphering functional tumor heterogeneity.
source: This growing body of evidence suggests that tumor cell behavior, as captured by BEHAV3D-TP, may serve as a predictive tool for deciphering functional tumor heterogeneity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential utility of BEHAV3D-TP.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP allows for the selection of diverse feature types, supporting datasets that include both dynamic, morphological, spatial, and environmental parameters.
source: In addition to motility-based classification, features such as tumor cell morphology, proliferation state, and interactions with the TME can further refine tumor phenotyping. BEHAV3D-TP allows for the selection of diverse feature types, supporting datasets that include both dynamic, morphological, spatial, and environmental parameters.
evidence: This describes a capability of BEHAV3D-TP.

claim: Expanding the feature set may introduce biologically irrelevant noise, particularly in 3D microscopy data where limited z-axis resolution can lead to morphological artifacts.
source: However, we recognize that expanding the feature set may introduce biologically irrelevant noise, particularly in 3D microscopy data where limited z-axis resolution can lead to morphological artifacts.
evidence: This is a recognition of a potential limitation.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP has been incorporated in a Google Colab notebook, allowing researchers with minimal programming skills to employ the tool online.
source: To enhance the accessibility of BEHAV3D-TP for researchers keen on studying tumor cell behavioral profiles through live imaging, we have incorporated our software in a Google Colab notebook, allowing researchers with minimal programming skills to employ the tool online without the requirement to install specific software environments nor the need to directly interact with the code.
evidence: This describes the implementation of BEHAV3D-TP.

claim: Google Colab provides the necessary computational resources to be able to run the pipeline without demanding a powerful local machine.
source: Google Colab provides the necessary computational resources to be able to run the pipeline without demanding a powerful local machine.
evidence: This describes a benefit of using Google Colab.

claim: There are RAM usage and runtime limitations that could affect the analysis in the free version of Google Colab.
source: However, there are RAM usage and runtime limitations that could affect the analysis, given a big enough dataset in the free version of Google Colab.
evidence: This describes a limitation of using the free version of Google Colab.

claim: The workflow can also be run locally via a Jupyter Notebook that can be downloaded from the Google Colab notebook.
source: Given this and data privacy concerns, the workflow can also be run locally via a Jupyter Notebook that can be downloaded from the Google Colab notebook.
evidence: This describes an alternative way to run BEHAV3D-TP.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP includes additional features such as directionality metrics crucial for invasion studies, detailed analysis of identified behavioral populations, data back-projection, and correlation of these behaviors with both large-scale and small-scale TME features.
source: While CellTracksColab offers valuable insights into tracking data, BEHAV3D-TP is specifically designed for IVM data and includes additional features. These features include directionality metrics crucial for invasion studies, detailed analysis of identified behavioral populations, data back-projection, and correlation of these behaviors with both large-scale and small-scale TME features.
evidence: This describes features of BEHAV3D-TP that distinguish it from CellTracksColab.

claim: BEHAV3D-TP provides a comprehensive approach that provides a deeper understanding of the TME drivers behind intratumoral heterogeneity.
source: This comprehensive approach provides a deeper understanding of the TME drivers behind intratumoral heterogeneity, making BEHAV3D-TP a robust tool for researchers investigating the complex behaviors of tumor cells in their natural environments.
evidence: This is a claim about the utility of BEHAV3D-TP.

claim: DMG007 (HSJD-DIPG-007) cells were established from primary DMG material and provided by Dr. Ángel Montero Carcaboso.
source: DMG007 (HSJD-DIPG-007) cells, established from primary DMG material and provided by Dr. Ángel Montero Carcaboso (Sant Joan de Déu Barcelona Hospital), were authenticated by STR profiling and tested negative for mycoplasma contamination.
evidence: This describes the source and authentication of the cell line used.

claim: DMG007 cells were authenticated by STR profiling and tested negative for mycoplasma contamination.
source: DMG007 (HSJD-DIPG-007) cells, established from primary DMG material and provided by Dr. Ángel Montero Carcaboso (Sant Joan de Déu Barcelona Hospital), were authenticated by STR profiling and tested negative for mycoplasma contamination.
evidence: This describes the authentication and quality control of the cell line used.

claim: Experiments were conducted in accordance with Institutional Guidelines and current Dutch laws on Animal Experimentation, with approval from the local Ethical Committee.
source: Experiments were conducted in accordance with Institutional Guidelines and current Dutch laws on Animal Experimentation, with approval from the local Ethical Committee (Animal Welfare Body of the Princess Máxima Center for Pediatric Oncology) and under CCD license AVD39900 202216507, following both local and international regulations.
evidence: This describes the ethical approval for the animal experiments.

claim: SR101 is a fluorescent marker known to label oligodendrocytes and astrocytes.
source: For in vivo TME labeling, we injected mice with an anti-CD31-AF647 antibody to label blood vessels, and with either SR101, a fluorescent marker known to label oligodendrocytes and astrocytes (Appaix et al., 2012; Rasmussen et al., 2016; Hagos and Hülsmann, 2016; Kim et al., 2019), or CD20r, a novel molecule described to label microglial cells (Liu et al., 2022; Figure 4—figure supplement 1a, b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CD20r is a novel molecule described to label microglial cells.
source: For in vivo TME labeling, we injected mice with an anti-CD31-AF647 antibody to label blood vessels, and with either SR101, a fluorescent marker known to label oligodendrocytes and astrocytes (Appaix et al., 2012; Rasmussen et al., 2016; Hagos and Hülsmann, 2016; Kim et al., 2019), or CD20r, a novel molecule described to label microglial cells (Liu et al., 2022; Figure 4—figure supplement 1a, b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The complete workflow—combining heterogeneity analysis with large- and small-scale phenotyping—is primarily optimized for datasets processed with Imaris.
source: The complete workflow—combining heterogeneity analysis with large- and small-scale phenotyping—is primarily optimized for datasets processed with Imaris due to its wide use in the IVM community and special suitability for 3D visualization and tracking.
evidence: This describes the optimization of BEHAV3D-TP for Imaris data.

claim: The core Heterogeneity module of BEHAV3D-TP is also compatible with Fiji-based tracking data, specifically outputs generated by TrackMate, MTrackJ and ManualTracking.
source: In addition, to broaden accessibility and support alternative data processing pipelines, the core Heterogeneity module of BEHAV3D-TP is also compatible with Fiji-based tracking data, specifically outputs generated by TrackMate. MTrackJ and ManualTracking.
evidence: This describes the compatibility of BEHAV3D-TP with Fiji-based tracking data.

claim: Linear interpolation was used to estimate the values of missing time points.
source: To account for missing time points and to create a time series with the same time interval for each tumor cell time series, linear interpolation was used to estimate the values of missing time points.
evidence: This describes a data processing step in the Heterogeneity module.

claim: Tracks were cropped to the minimal common length among all tracks.
source: To compare time series independently, tracks were cropped to the minimal common length among all tracks. In the case of DMG data to a 2.6 hr duration.
evidence: This describes a data processing step in the Heterogeneity module.

claim: Principal component analysis was performed and the number of PCs that explained at least 90% of data variance (3) were selected.
source: First, we performed a principal component (PC) analysis and selected the number of PCs that explained at least 90% of data variance (3).
evidence: This describes a data processing step in the Heterogeneity module.

claim: The cross-distance matrix between each tumor cell multivariate time series was computed using the dynamic time warping algorithm from the package 'dtwclust'.
source: The previously calculated PCs were then used to compute the cross-distance matrix between each tumor cell multivariate time series using the dynamic time warping algorithm from the package 'dtwclust'.
evidence: This describes a data processing step in the Heterogeneity module.

claim: Dimensionality reduction on the cross-distance matrix was performed by the Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection method ('umap' package).
source: To visualize heterogeneous tumor cell behaviors in two dimensions, dimensionality reduction on the cross-distance matrix was performed by the Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection method ('umap' package).
evidence: This describes a data processing step in the Heterogeneity module.

claim: Clustering was performed using the k-means clustering algorithm.
source: Clustering was performed using the k-means clustering algorithm.
evidence: This describes a data processing step in the Heterogeneity module.

claim: DMG cells located within 15 µm of TAMM surfaces were classified as 'close' to CD20r+ TAMMs.
source: To quantify the percentage of DMG cells in proximity to CD20r+ TAMMs, we classified cells located within 15  µm of TAMM surfaces as 'close'.
evidence: This describes a data processing step in the Small-scale phenotyping module.

claim: DMG cells were considered 'close' to blood vessels if they were within 3 µm of blood vessel spots.
source: For proximity to blood vessels, DMG cells were considered 'close' if they were within 3  µm of blood vessel spots.
evidence: This describes a data processing step in the Small-scale phenotyping module.

claim: Two-tailed unpaired t-tests were performed for comparison between two groups in Figure 1—figure supplement 1d.
source: Two-tailed unpaired t-tests were performed for comparison between two groups in Figure 1—figure supplement 1d.
evidence: This describes a statistical method used.

claim: For comparisons involving more than two groups, where no random effects were present, one-way ANOVA was performed, followed by Tukey's Honest Significant Difference post hoc test.
source: For comparisons involving more than two groups, where no random effects were present, we performed one-way ANOVA (Figures 2d and 4b), followed by Tukey's Honest Significant Difference post hoc test to correct for multiple comparisons.
evidence: This describes a statistical method used.

claim: A linear mixed-effects model with mouse and/or TME class included as random effects was applied where necessary to account for inter-mouse and TME region variability.
source: Where necessary to account for inter-mouse and TME region variability, we applied a linear mixed-effects model with mouse and/or TME class included as random effects (Figure 4c, e, Figure 1—figure supplement 3d, Figure 4—figure supplement 1c and d).
evidence: This describes a statistical method used.

claim: A Chi-square test was performed to compare the distribution of different morphodynamic clusters of TEB cells.
source: To compare the distribution of different morphodynamic clusters of TEB cells, we pooled all positions and mice due to the low number of cells per position. We then constructed a contingency table and performed a Chi-square test (Figure 1—figure supplement 2d).
evidence: This describes a statistical method used.
